definition: Brazen means excessively bold and without shame — daring done openly, as if unable to blush.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word brazen. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know brazen should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Even his own teammates laughed at the brazen dive: the striker went down clutching his shin before the defender had touched him.
Bold is milder than brazen: a bold plan takes a real risk, but it can still be modest about it.
Shameless goes a step further than brazen — brazen defiance still performs for an audience it means to shock; shameless has stopped caring whether anyone watches at all.

Brash is pushy boldness with no polish or patience — barging in loud, heedless of how it lands. Brazen keeps the nerve but adds shameless display: a brazen act is performed in the open and dares onlookers to object. Brash blunders forward; brazen performs.

Defiant means openly resisting a rule or an authority — a defiant refusal, a defiant stare at the referee. Brazen needs no authority to resist: it names boldness that has lost its shame, offensive in itself even when no rule forbids it.

Professor Idris Halloran had graded thousands of essays, but the one on his desk that October achieved something new: it was his own published article, retitled and turned in to him.
The student had not even changed the examples.
When Halloran called him in, he expected excuses — a mix-up, a wrong file.
Instead the young man leaned back and asked, 'Can you prove it?' — with the journal in question visible on the shelf behind Halloran's head.
Colleagues, hearing the story, kept using the same word: brazen.
Not sneaky, not desperate — theft carried out in the open, daring its victim to object.
The dean's hearing took eleven minutes.
The student's only regret, he said on the way out, was the grade.
